card: This PR checks the compiled AssumeUTXO snapshot hash during standard Initial Block Download once block connection reaches the snapshot height. Reconstructed UTXO state is hashed after flushing to disk; if the hash fails to match the commitment, the node logs the error and raises a GUI and RPC warning without aborting IBD. Nodes syncing from genesis previously never validated baked-in snapshot commitments against the actual chain history (#32377). To avoid multiple multi-minute hashing operations during sync, each network retains only the latest AssumeUTXO commitment, deprecating older snapshots.
changed_since_previous: A commitment mismatch during IBD no longer triggers a fatal error and node shutdown; it now logs an error and issues a non-fatal GUI/RPC warning so ordinary sync can proceed. UTXO hashing interruptions during shutdown are also explicitly distinguished from verification failures.
evidence: PR description references issue #32377: 'AssumeUTXO: crowdsource trust through independent snapshot verification'.
Commit f98aca5b8f notes this 'checks the developer-provided commitment against the UTXO set that every node reconstructs during IBD'.
problem: AssumeUTXO relies on hardcoded snapshot hashes baked into the release binary. Even though standard nodes independently construct the UTXO set from genesis during IBD, they never check their reconstructed state against the compiled commitment, missing an opportunity for crowdsourced verification of baked-in snapshot data (#32377).

risk.why: Forcing a UTXO flush and multi-minute hash calculation synchronously during block connection could stall or crash node synchronization at the snapshot height if flush or interrupt handling fails.

scope_notes: Retaining only the latest snapshot commitment is a breaking change for loading older snapshots with loadtxoutset; the release notes document that older snapshots now require compiling with the older commitment restored.
summary: Verifies the compiled AssumeUTXO commitment during normal Initial Block Download when block connection reaches the commitment block. Pending UTXO changes are flushed to disk to hash the serialized UTXO set, and any mismatch logs an error and sets a GUI and RPC warning while allowing IBD to continue. To limit the performance cost of hashing during IBD, chainparams is changed to retain only the single most recent AssumeUTXO commitment per network, retiring support for loading older snapshots.
